question: Under Alabama law, which of these activities may NOT be performed for a fee unless the person holds an Alabama real estate license?
choice_a: Preparing a comparative market analysis for one's own personal residence
choice_b: Negotiating or attempting to negotiate the sale, exchange, purchase, rental, or lease of real estate situated in Alabama
choice_c: Referring a friend to a licensed agent without receiving anything of value
choice_d: Advertising one's own home for sale by owner
explanation: Section 34-27-30 makes it unlawful to sell, exchange, negotiate, list, auction, or otherwise deal in real estate for a fee or commission without an Alabama real estate license. The other options involve no compensation-based real estate activity performed for another party.

question: Under Section 34-27-30(10), a person who merely presents himself or herself, or is presented, as being able to perform an act for which a license is required...
choice_a: Is exempt as long as no fee ultimately changes hands
choice_b: Only needs a license if a transaction later closes
choice_c: Must be licensed even if no transaction is ever actually completed
choice_d: Is exempt if the person clearly discloses that he or she is unlicensed
explanation: Section 34-27-30(10) separately criminalizes simply holding oneself out as able to perform licensed activities, regardless of whether a transaction is completed or a fee is collected.

question: Which of the following persons is exempt from Alabama real estate licensing requirements under Section 34-27-2(b)(1)?
choice_a: A property manager hired by an unrelated owner to lease out a rental home
choice_b: A licensed salesperson who helps a friend sell a home in exchange for a referral fee
choice_c: A corporate officer with no authority over the corporation's policy decisions who is asked to sign a listing
choice_d: An owner managing or selling his or her own real estate, or that of a spouse, child, or parent
explanation: The owner exemption covers a person managing or consummating a transaction involving his or her own property (or that of a spouse, child, or parent). Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.03(2) clarifies that for a corporation or partnership, "owner" means a partner or corporate officer who actually has authority over overall policy — someone without that authority does not qualify for the exemption.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-2(b)(1); Ala. Admin. Code r. 790-X-1-.03(2)

question: An attorney-at-law in Alabama who negotiates terms of a real estate closing while performing his or her duties as an attorney...
choice_a: Is exempt from Alabama real estate licensing requirements while performing attorney duties
choice_b: Must hold an inactive real estate license as a backup credential
choice_c: Must obtain a temporary salesperson license before the closing
choice_d: Is only exempt from licensure if the client is a spouse or other relative
explanation: Section 34-27-2(b)(2) exempts an attorney-at-law from real estate licensing requirements when performing his or her duties as an attorney-at-law.

question: A person acting under a duly executed power of attorney to consummate a real estate transaction for someone else is exempt from Alabama real estate licensure only if that person...
choice_a: Is related to the property owner by blood
choice_b: Acts without compensation and in good faith
choice_c: Limits the power of attorney to a single parcel
choice_d: Files the power of attorney with the Alabama Real Estate Commission
explanation: Section 34-27-2(b)(3) exempts persons acting without compensation and in good faith under a duly executed power of attorney authorizing a real estate transaction. Receiving compensation removes the exemption.

question: Under Alabama's licensing exemptions, which of the following managers is NOT exempt from real estate licensure?
choice_a: A manager of a conventional apartment building or complex
choice_b: A person performing general clerical duties for a broker who never shows listed property
choice_c: An on-site manager of a condominium building or complex
choice_d: An attorney-at-law performing attorney duties
explanation: Section 34-27-2(b)(7) exempts persons acting as the manager of an apartment building or complex, but the statute expressly states this exception does NOT apply to a person acting as an on-site manager of a condominium building or complex.

question: During a licensed real estate auction in Alabama, a "ground man" whose role is limited to relaying crowd participation bids to the licensed auctioneer...
choice_a: Must hold at least a temporary salesperson license
choice_b: Must be licensed as a full broker
choice_c: May only work under a written co-brokerage agreement
choice_d: Is not required to hold a real estate license
explanation: Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.03(4) clarifies that while auctioning real estate generally requires a license under § 34-27-30(5), "ground men" whose activities are limited to relaying crowd bids to the auctioneer are not required to be licensed.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.03(1), which rental-related activity triggers the requirement to hold a real estate license?
choice_a: Entering into an agreement to collect and hold in escrow rental payments for property situated in Alabama
choice_b: Performing routine maintenance repairs on a rental unit at the owner's request
choice_c: Handing new tenants their keys on move-in day
choice_d: Mowing the lawn of a vacant rental property between tenants
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.03(1) lists activities constituting rental leasing and/or property management requiring licensure, including contracting for the collection and escrow of security deposits and rental payments for Alabama property. Purely physical maintenance or custodial tasks are not licensed activities.

question: A written co-brokerage agreement between a licensed principal broker of another state and an Alabama qualifying broker is limited to how many transactions per calendar year, per out-of-state principal broker?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Three
choice_c: Five
choice_d: There is no numerical limit on transactions
explanation: Section 34-27-3(a)(3) limits a co-brokerage agreement to three transactions per calendar year per licensed out-of-state principal broker (a transaction may include multiple properties if part of the same portfolio).

question: Under Alabama's co-brokerage statute, the total dollar volume of Alabama transactions an out-of-state principal broker may conduct under co-brokerage agreements in a single calendar year is capped at:
choice_d: There is no dollar cap, only a transaction-count cap
explanation: Section 34-27-3(a)(4) prohibits an out-of-state principal broker from using co-brokerage agreements to engage in Alabama transactions totaling more than $50,000,000 in any calendar year.

question: After an Alabama qualifying broker signs a co-brokerage agreement with an out-of-state principal broker, within how many days must the Alabama broker file a copy of the agreement with the Commission?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 5 days
choice_c: 60 days
choice_d: 10 days
explanation: Section 34-27-3(b) requires the Alabama qualifying broker to file a copy of each written co-brokerage agreement with the Commission not more than 10 days after it is signed by all parties.

question: Under a co-brokerage agreement covering Alabama property, who is responsible for supervising the showing of the property and any subsequent negotiations?
choice_a: The Alabama qualifying broker
choice_b: The out-of-state principal broker
choice_c: Whichever broker the buyer selects
choice_d: The buyer's or seller's attorney
explanation: Section 34-27-3(c)(3) requires that an Alabama broker supervise the showing of property located in Alabama and any subsequent negotiations; Rule 790-X-1-.05(2) restates this supervisory duty.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-3(c)(3); Ala. Admin. Code r. 790-X-1-.05(2)

question: In an Alabama co-brokerage transaction, earnest money deposited under the agreement must be held in escrow by the Alabama qualifying broker unless:
choice_a: The out-of-state broker requests to hold the funds instead
choice_b: Both the buyer and the seller agree in writing to relieve the Alabama broker of that responsibility
choice_c: The property is valued above $1,000,000
choice_d: The transaction is scheduled to close within 10 days
explanation: Section 34-27-3(c)(6) requires that earnest money deposited under a co-brokerage agreement be held in escrow by the Alabama qualifying broker unless both buyer and seller agree in writing to relieve the Alabama broker of that responsibility.

question: Under Section 34-27-3(c)(4), whose name must appear in all advertising of Alabama real property that is subject to a co-brokerage agreement?
choice_a: Only the out-of-state broker's name
choice_b: Only the individual listing agent's personal name
choice_c: The Alabama qualifying broker's name
choice_d: Advertising is not required to name either broker
explanation: Section 34-27-3(c)(4) requires that the name of the Alabama broker appear in all advertising of real property located in the state that is subject to a co-brokerage agreement.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.05(3), when an Alabama qualifying broker enters into a co-brokerage agreement with an out-of-state broker, the Alabama broker is liable for:
choice_a: Only the Alabama broker's own acts, never the out-of-state broker's acts
choice_b: Only acts that occur after the transaction closes
choice_c: Nothing, because liability passes entirely to the out-of-state broker
choice_d: All acts of the out-of-state broker arising from the co-brokerage agreement, as well as the Alabama broker's own acts
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.05(3) makes the Alabama qualifying broker liable for all acts of the out-of-state broker arising from execution of the co-brokerage agreement, in addition to the Alabama broker's own acts.

question: To qualify for an original Alabama real estate license, an applicant must be at least:
choice_a: 19 years of age
choice_b: 18 years of age
choice_c: 21 years of age
choice_d: 20 years of age
explanation: Section 34-27-32(a)(4) requires that an applicant for a broker's or salesperson's license be at least 19 years of age.

question: Under Section 34-27-32(a)(3), an applicant whose real estate license was revoked in any state (including Alabama) within the two years preceding the Alabama application...
choice_a: Is permanently and irrevocably barred from Alabama licensure
choice_b: May not be issued an Alabama license without the approval of the commissioners
choice_c: May be licensed automatically after paying an additional penalty fee
choice_d: Is unaffected, because out-of-state revocations do not matter in Alabama
explanation: Section 34-27-32(a)(3) bars issuance of an Alabama license to a person whose license was revoked in any state within the prior two years, unless the commissioners approve; revocations older than two years do not trigger this bar.

question: Under Section 34-27-32(a)(2), an applicant whose application for a real estate license was rejected in another state for reasons other than failing a written exam, within the past two years...
choice_a: Must simply retake and pass the Alabama licensing exam to override the rejection
choice_b: Is exempt from this rule if the rejection occurred more than six months ago
choice_c: May not be issued an Alabama real estate license without approval of the commissioners
choice_d: Is unaffected because only revocations, not rejections, matter under Alabama law
explanation: Section 34-27-32(a)(2) treats a recent (within two years) license rejection in another state — for any reason other than failing a written exam — the same way as a revocation: it bars an Alabama license absent commissioner approval.

question: A nonresident applicant for an Alabama real estate license must sign an affidavit agreeing to which of the following?
choice_a: That the applicant will maintain a physical office located in Alabama
choice_b: That the applicant waives all rights to a hearing before the Commission
choice_c: That the applicant will only represent Alabama-resident buyers and sellers
choice_d: That the Alabama Real Estate Commission has jurisdiction over the applicant's real estate activities the same as if the applicant were an Alabama resident licensee
explanation: Section 34-27-32(a)(6) requires nonresident applicants to sign an affidavit consenting to Commission jurisdiction, agreeing to appoint the Executive Director (or Assistant Executive Director) as agent for service of process, and agreeing to be bound by Alabama license law the same as a resident.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-2-.01(5), an applicant for an original salesperson or broker license (who is not applying for a reciprocal license) must generally provide proof of:
choice_a: High school graduation or an equivalent such as a GED certificate
choice_b: A completed four-year college degree
choice_c: At least two years of prior sales experience
choice_d: Current membership in a local Realtor association
explanation: Rule 790-X-2-.01(5) requires applicants who completed high school in the United States (other than reciprocal or home-schooled applicants) to show proof of graduation via a diploma, transcript, GED certificate, or similar document.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-2-.01(1), applicants must document that they meet the minimum age requirement using which type of proof?
choice_a: A notarized personal statement affirming their age with no supporting document
choice_b: A valid driver's license, U.S. passport, birth certificate, or other Commission-acceptable documentation
choice_c: A Social Security card only
choice_d: A signed statement from the applicant's qualifying broker
explanation: Rule 790-X-2-.01(1) requires all applicants to document that they are at least 19 years of age using a valid driver's license, U.S. passport, birth certificate, or other documentation acceptable to the Commission.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-2-.01(3), an applicant must document his or her state of residence with which type of proof?
choice_a: A letter from the applicant's employer confirming residency
choice_b: A utility bill only, with no other documents accepted
choice_c: A current driver's license, car tag receipt, deed, lease, property tax bill, voter registration card, or similar document
choice_d: Proof of residency is not required for original licensure
explanation: Rule 790-X-2-.01(3) lists acceptable residency documents, including a current driver's license, car tag receipt, deed, lease agreement, property tax bill, or voter registration card.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-2-.01(7), an applicant who completed high school outside the United States must provide:
choice_a: Nothing further, since foreign education is automatically accepted
choice_b: Proof that the applicant has since become a U.S. citizen
choice_c: A letter from the Alabama Department of Education certifying equivalency
choice_d: A transcript or diploma from a U.S. college verifying sufficient education for post-secondary admission, or a translated transcript/diploma from the foreign high school or college attended
explanation: Rule 790-X-2-.01(7) requires applicants educated outside the U.S. to submit either a U.S. college record showing sufficient foreign secondary education for post-secondary admission, or an English-translated transcript or diploma from the foreign school attended.

question: An Alabama real estate license renewal form and renewal fees must be filed on or before what date to renew the license on a timely basis?
choice_a: August 31 of the final year of the license period
choice_b: September 30 of the final year of the license period
choice_c: October 1 of the next license period
choice_d: July 1 of the final year of the license period
explanation: Section 34-27-35(g) requires the renewal form and fees to be filed on or before August 31 of the final year of each license period for timely renewal into the following license period.

question: Under Section 34-27-35(g), a licensee who files for renewal between September 1 and September 30 of the final year of the license period must pay the renewal fee plus a penalty of:
explanation: Section 34-27-35(g) imposes a $150 penalty, in addition to the ordinary renewal fees, for renewals filed during the September 1 through September 30 grace window of the final license year.

question: By what date must the Alabama Real Estate Commission mail the license renewal form to a licensee's business (if active) or residence (if inactive) address?
choice_a: Prior to July 1 of the final year of the license period
choice_b: Prior to September 1 of the final year of the license period
choice_c: Prior to August 1 of the final year of the license period
choice_d: There is no statutory mailing deadline
explanation: Section 34-27-35(h) requires the Commission to mail the renewal form to the licensee's address of record prior to August 1 of the final year of each license period.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-2-.16(1), if a licensee does not receive a renewal notice from the Commission, the licensee is responsible for notifying the Commission of that failure by what date?
choice_a: September 30 of the renewal period
choice_b: October 1 of the new license period
choice_c: There is no such notification duty on the licensee
choice_d: August 10 of the renewal period
explanation: Rule 790-X-2-.16(1) places the burden on the licensee to notify the Commission by August 10 of the renewal period if a renewal form was not received, rather than allowing the licensee to simply wait.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-2-.16(2), a standard license renewal form may be used to accomplish which of the following?
choice_a: Only the renewal of an existing license — any change constituting a transfer must be submitted through separate transfer procedures
choice_b: Both renewal and a simultaneous change of qualifying broker
choice_c: Renewal, transfer, and reactivation, all on the same form
choice_d: Renewal of a company license but not an individual license
explanation: Rule 790-X-2-.16(2) limits the renewal form to effecting only the renewal of a license; any changes that constitute a transfer (such as a change of qualifying broker or address) must be submitted using the Commission's established transfer procedures instead.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-2-.26, a licensee who is on current military deployment at the time of license renewal may, upon providing deployment papers:
choice_a: Automatically have the license permanently exempted from all future continuing education
choice_b: Have license renewal deferred and continuing education waived for the period of deployment
choice_c: Have the license immediately upgraded to inactive-exempt status with no further obligations
choice_d: Only defer the renewal fee, while continuing education remains due on the normal schedule
explanation: Rule 790-X-2-.26 allows deployed military licensees to defer renewal and waive continuing education for the deployment period, provided the licensee later completes the deferred renewal and previously waived CE by December 31 of the year following the end of deployment.

question: Under Section 34-27-35(b), the Alabama Real Estate Commission has authority to establish a license period of:
choice_a: Exactly one year, with no other option allowed by statute
choice_b: Exactly five years for all license types
choice_c: One year or multiple years, at the Commission's discretion
choice_d: A license period tied to each individual licensee's birth date
explanation: Section 34-27-35(b) provides that the Commission may establish a one-year or multi-year license period.

question: To renew an active Alabama salesperson or broker license, an applicant must submit proof of completion of not less than how many clock hours of approved continuing education?
choice_a: 8 clock hours
choice_b: 30 clock hours
choice_c: 6 clock hours
choice_d: 15 clock hours
explanation: Section 34-27-35(j)(1) requires proof of completion of not less than 15 clock hours of approved continuing education coursework for each renewal of an active salesperson or broker license.

question: Effective October 1, 2022, an Alabama associate broker's or qualifying broker's 15-hour continuing education requirement each license period must include:
choice_a: 3 clock hours of Risk Management, 3 clock hours of a Commission-approved Broker course, and 9 clock hours of Commission-approved elective courses
choice_b: 15 clock hours of any elective coursework, with no required subject matter
choice_c: 3 clock hours of Risk Management and 12 clock hours of elective courses (the same formula as salespersons)
choice_d: 6 clock hours of Risk Management and 9 clock hours of elective courses
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.11(2) sets a broker-specific continuing education formula, effective October 1, 2022: 3 hours Risk Management, 3 hours a Commission-approved Broker course, and 9 hours of Commission-approved courses — distinct from the salesperson formula.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.11(1), a salesperson's 15-hour continuing education requirement each license period must include:
choice_a: 3 clock hours Risk Management, 3 clock hours Broker course, and 9 clock hours elective (the broker formula)
choice_b: 3 clock hours in a Commission-approved Risk Management course and 12 clock hours in Commission-approved courses
choice_c: 15 clock hours entirely of the licensee's own choosing, with no required course
choice_d: 6 clock hours Risk Management and 9 clock hours of elective courses
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.11(1) requires salespersons to complete 3 hours of Risk Management plus 12 hours of other Commission-approved coursework, which differs from the broker-specific 3/3/9 breakdown under paragraph (2).

question: Under Section 34-27-35(j)(2), a licensee applying for the first renewal of a license held for not more than one year...
choice_a: Must complete double the standard continuing education hours instead
choice_b: Must retake the full licensing examination in lieu of continuing education
choice_c: Is not required to comply with the continuing education requirement for that first renewal
choice_d: Is ineligible to renew until the standard exemption period passes
explanation: Section 34-27-35(j)(2) exempts a first-time renewal applicant who has held the license for no more than one year from the continuing education requirement for that particular renewal.

question: Under Section 34-27-35(j), service as a member of the Alabama State Legislature during a license renewal period is treated as:
choice_a: Grounds for automatic disciplinary action against the licensee
choice_b: Irrelevant to the licensee's continuing education obligation
choice_c: Equivalent to only half of the required continuing education hours
choice_d: The equivalent of the 15-hour continuing education requirement
explanation: Section 34-27-35(j) specifically deems time served as a member of the state Legislature during a license renewal period to be the equivalent of the required 15 hours of continuing education coursework.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.12(3), a licensee may not earn more than how many hours of continuing education credit in any single day?
choice_a: 9 hours
choice_b: 15 hours
choice_c: 6 hours
choice_d: 12 hours
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.12(3) caps continuing education credit at 9 hours per day, and also requires each approved course to contain a minimum of 3 clock hours of instruction.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.12(8), what portion of a continuing education class may be presented through video, unless the course is an ARELLO-certified distance education course?
choice_a: Up to one-half of the class
choice_b: No more than one-third of the class
choice_c: Up to 100% of the class — video presentation is unrestricted
choice_d: No video is permitted under any circumstance
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.12(8) limits video presentation to no more than one-third of any continuing education class, unless the course is ARELLO-certified distance education.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.12(9), what percentage of a continuing education course must a licensee attend in order to receive credit?
choice_a: 90% of the course offering
choice_b: 80% of the course offering
choice_c: 100% of the course offering
choice_d: 75% of the course offering
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.12(9) requires 100% attendance of a continuing education course to receive credit — a stricter standard than the 90% attendance rule that applies to prelicense and post-license courses.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.12(10), a licensee who completes the entire 60-hour broker prelicense course or the entire 30-hour post-license course automatically earns:
choice_a: No continuing education credit — CE must always be earned through separate CE-specific courses
choice_b: 30 clock hours of continuing education credit
choice_c: Credit that may only be applied toward the following license period, not the current one
choice_d: 15 clock hours of continuing education credit, satisfying all continuing education requirements for the current license period
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.12(10) grants 15 clock hours of continuing education credit to any licensee completing the full 60-hour broker prelicense course or the full 30-hour post-license course, fully satisfying CE for that license period.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.11(3), which subject matter is explicitly identified as NOT acceptable for continuing education elective credit?
choice_a: Motivational courses and personal development courses
choice_b: Real estate financing
choice_c: Fair housing
choice_d: Agency disclosure
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.11(3) lists acceptable "core" real estate subjects (financing, fair housing, agency disclosure, ethics, etc.) but expressly excludes motivational courses, personal development courses, sales meetings, in-house training, and orientation courses.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.09(6), a person seeking approval as a continuing education instructor based solely on full-time occupational experience (without a bachelor's degree or teaching-experience combination) must show at least:
choice_a: Two years of full-time experience in the field of instruction
choice_b: Six years of full-time experience in the profession, trade, or occupation in the field of instruction
choice_c: Ten years of full-time experience in the field of instruction
choice_d: One year of full-time experience plus a letter of recommendation
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.09(6)(c) allows qualification through six years of full-time experience in the applicable profession, trade, or occupation, as one of several alternative qualification paths for continuing education instructors.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.09(8), a continuing education instructor who teaches an approved CE course...
choice_a: Automatically earns double continuing education credit for teaching
choice_b: Earns the standard 15-hour CE credit for teaching any single course
choice_c: Does not earn continuing education credit for teaching that course
choice_d: May apply teaching hours toward instructor training requirements instead of CE
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.09(8) specifically states that continuing education instructors shall not earn continuing education credit for teaching courses.

question: The holder of a temporary Alabama salesperson license must complete a post-license course of how many clock hours before an original (permanent) license can be issued?
choice_a: 60 clock hours
choice_b: 15 clock hours
choice_c: 45 clock hours
choice_d: 30 clock hours
explanation: Section 34-27-33(c)(2) requires the holder of a temporary license to satisfactorily complete a 30-hour post-license course prescribed by the Commission before an original license may be issued.

question: To maintain an active license, the holder of a temporary salesperson license must complete the post-license course and have the original license issued within:
choice_a: The first six months of licensure
choice_b: The first three months of licensure
choice_c: The full one-year period, with no earlier deadline for active status
choice_d: 90 days of passing the licensing examination
explanation: Section 34-27-33(c)(2) requires completion of the post-license course and issuance of the original license within the first six months of the temporary license, or the temporary license is automatically placed on inactive status.

question: Under Section 34-27-33(c)(4), a licensee who satisfactorily completes the post-license course and receives an original license is exempt from continuing education requirements for:
choice_a: The first two renewals of the original license
choice_b: The first renewal of the original license only
choice_c: The entire first five years of licensure
choice_d: There is no continuing-education exemption tied to the post-license course
explanation: Section 34-27-33(c)(4) exempts a licensee who has completed the post-license course from the continuing education requirement only for the first renewal of the original license — subsequent renewals require the standard 15 CE hours.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.06(l), before a temporary salesperson may enroll in the 30-hour post-license course, the school must first obtain:
choice_a: A signed listing agreement from the student's sponsoring qualifying broker
choice_b: Proof of the student's high school diploma
choice_c: The student's temporary license number
choice_d: A written letter of recommendation from the student's qualifying broker
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.06(l) requires a temporary license to be issued before a person begins the post-license course, and instructors/administrators must obtain the temporary license number before allowing enrollment.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.06(f), what minimum percentage of course hours in prelicense and post-license courses must be presented through live instruction, unless the course is an ARELLO-certified distance education course?
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.06(f) requires that at least 80% of course hours in prelicense and post-license courses be presented through live instruction, absent an ARELLO-certified distance education course.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.06(g)-(i), to successfully complete the salesperson prelicense course, a student must pass all required incremental assessments, pass the final course exam, and achieve a minimum course grade of:
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.06(g) and (i) require students to pass all incremental assessments and the final course exam while achieving a minimum overall course grade of 70% to successfully complete the salesperson prelicense course (the same 70% minimum applies to the broker prelicense course under paragraph (k)).

question: A temporary Alabama salesperson license is valid for a maximum period of:
choice_a: Six months following its issuance
choice_b: One year following the first day of the month after its issuance
choice_c: Two years following its issuance
choice_d: 90 days following its issuance
explanation: Section 34-27-33(c)(1) provides that a temporary license is valid only for a period of one year following the first day of the month after its issuance.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-2-.03, a temporary salesperson license may remain on ACTIVE status for only:
choice_a: The full one-year period during which it is valid
choice_b: The first 90 days following its issuance
choice_c: The first six months following its issuance
choice_d: Until the post-license course begins, regardless of how long that takes
explanation: Rule 790-X-2-.03(2)-(3) provides that a temporary salesperson license is on active status only for the first six months after issuance; during the remaining six months of its one-year validity, it can only be on inactive status while the holder completes the post-license course.

question: If the holder of a temporary salesperson license fails to complete the post-license course and obtain an original license within one year of issuance, the temporary license:
choice_a: Automatically converts to an inactive broker's license
choice_b: Remains valid indefinitely until affirmatively revoked
choice_c: Is automatically renewed for one additional year
choice_d: Automatically expires and lapses
explanation: Under Section 34-27-33(c)(2) and Rule 790-X-2-.03(2), a temporary license that is not converted to an original license (via completion of the post-license course) within the one-year validity period automatically expires and lapses.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-33(c)(2); Ala. Admin. Code r. 790-X-2-.03(2)

question: Under Section 34-27-33(c)(3), an applicant who has already paid the Recovery Fund fee to obtain a temporary salesperson license, and later completes the post-license course to obtain the original license, must:
choice_a: Not pay another Recovery Fund fee in order to have the original license issued
choice_b: Pay the Recovery Fund fee a second time before the original license issues
choice_c: Pay double the standard Recovery Fund fee at the time of original licensure
choice_d: Pay the Recovery Fund fee again only if the applicant changed qualifying brokers
explanation: Section 34-27-33(c)(3) specifically provides that an applicant for an original license who already paid the Recovery Fund fee for the temporary license is not required to pay another Recovery Fund fee to obtain the original license — a different scenario from a salesperson later upgrading to a broker license.

question: A temporary salesperson license holder who wishes to change qualifying brokers during the first six months after issuance:
choice_a: May not change qualifying brokers under any circumstances while holding a temporary license
choice_b: May transfer the license using the Commission's regular transfer procedures
choice_c: Must wait until the original (permanent) license is issued before transferring
choice_d: Must apply for and be issued an entirely new temporary license
explanation: Rule 790-X-2-.03(4) allows a temporary salesperson license holder to transfer to a new qualifying broker via the regular transfer procedures at any time during the first six months after issuance of the temporary license.

question: Under Alabama Administrative Code Rule 790-X-1-.06(6), a salesperson applicant must pass the state salesperson licensing examination within what period following successful completion of the prelicense course, or be required to retake the course?
choice_a: Ninety days
choice_b: One year
choice_c: Six months
choice_d: Three months
explanation: Rule 790-X-1-.06(6) requires salesperson applicants to pass the license examination within six months of completing the prelicense course; failing to do so requires the applicant to again complete the prelicense course and pass the exam. The same six-month rule applies to broker applicants under paragraph (7).
